how.title: Three steps. No accounts required.
how.intro: shhnote encrypts your secret in the browser before anything touches the network. The encryption key lives in the URL fragment — a part of the URL that browsers never send to servers.

steps.title: Encrypt
steps.body: Your secret is encrypted on your own device before anything is sent. The key to unlock it is never uploaded.

steps.title: Share
steps.body: It lives in the part of the link after the # — which browsers keep local and never send to a server.

steps.title: Retrieve
steps.body: The recipient's browser unlocks it locally and the server destroys its copy. Even we can't recover it.

hood.title: The cryptography, spelled out.
hood.intro: No hand-waving. Here's exactly what protects your secret, and where each piece runs — so you can verify the claims instead of taking them on faith.

specs.label: Encryption
specs.body: Authenticated symmetric encryption. Every secret is sealed with a 256-bit key and an integrity tag, so tampering is detected — not just left unreadable.

specs.label: Key derivation
specs.body: Optional passphrases are stretched with a memory-hard KDF, making offline brute-force attacks slow and costly even on purpose-built hardware.

specs.label: Randomness
specs.body: Keys and nonces are drawn from the browser's cryptographically secure generator. Never Math.random(), never predictable.

specs.label: Key custody
specs.body: The decryption key rides after the # in your link. Browsers never transmit the fragment, so the key that unlocks the secret never reaches our servers.

specs.label: In transit
specs.body: Only ciphertext ever leaves your device, carried over modern TLS. What we receive is an opaque blob we have no way to open.

specs.label: At rest
specs.body: We persist an encrypted blob and an expiry timestamp — nothing else. No plaintext, no keys, no sender or recipient metadata.

items.label: DevOps & Engineering
items.title: Credentials & Keys
items.body: Stop pasting API keys, database passwords, and SSH keys into chat threads. Share them as one-time links that self-destruct after use. Integrate with CI/CD pipelines via the API.

items.label: Privacy-conscious users
items.title: Share without a trace
items.body: Works over Tor without degraded functionality. No CAPTCHAs, no browser fingerprinting, no external requests. Every font and asset is self-hosted. Zero metadata leakage.

items.label: IT & Onboarding
items.title: Provision access securely
items.body: Send new hires initial credentials, VPN configs, or Wi-Fi passwords without leaving traces in email threads or ticketing systems. Generate multiple unique links for batch onboarding.

items.label: Legal & Regulatory
items.title: Compliance-sensitive records
items.body: Send a patient record, case file, or financial statement to a client or colleague without it sitting in an inbox that's subject to discovery, audit, or breach disclosure.

items.label: Personal
items.title: Everyday secrets
items.body: Send your accountant tax document passwords. Share streaming credentials with family. Give a contractor your alarm code. Send sensitive files securely. Simple enough for anyone.

items.label: Misc
items.title: Gift codes or surprise reveals
items.body: Send a gift card code, a surprise, scavenger/treasure hunt clue, or a reveal that vanishes after they've seen it.

cta.title: Stop sharing sensitive info in plaintext
cta.intro: Create a one-time encrypted link in seconds. Or create a multi-view encrypted link that expires in a few hours or days. Add extra protection with a password. No account needed. No data collected.
